mainTopic: Swaying walls as מחיצות; the new משנה on who is exempt from סוכה, and the source for עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous page about whether a wall that sways in the wind can count as a מחיצה. In the case of a tree whose branches hang down, the branches were tied with הוצא ודפנא. The גמרא then asks why carrying there is limited to בית סאתים. It answers that the space is a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, a place used for the open area around it. A second challenge comes from a ברייתא about uncut grain surrounding a reaped field, and it is answered the same way: the stalks were tied. Then a new משנה teaches that שלוחי מצוה, the sick, and their caretakers are exempt from סוכה, and that casual eating may be done outside the סוכה. The גמרא learns the exemption for someone busy with a מצוה from the פסוק of קריאת שמע ('בשבתך… ובלכתך'), which also exempts a חתן who marries a בתולה. It explains that only distraction caused by a מצוה exempts a person, not personal distress like a sunken ship or mourning. Finally, the גמרא suggests the rule comes from a different source: the men who were טמא and missed the קרבן פסח. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why only בית סאתים if the branches are tied?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a question begun on the previous page. If the tree branches were tied down and count as a real מחיצה, why is carrying under the tree limited to a בית סאתים?
steps.simpleTranslation: [If so, why may one not carry under the tree] except within בית סאתים!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a challenge that started on the previous page. The גמרא asks: if the hanging branches were tied and are a real wall, why is carrying limited to a small area?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא explained that one may carry under the tree because the branches were tied with הוצא ודפנא, so they don't sway. A fully valid enclosure would normally allow carrying in any size area. So the limit of בית סאתים suggests something is still wrong with the enclosure.

keyTerms.meaning: An area large enough to plant two סאה of seed (about 5,000 square אמות, the size of the משכן courtyard). It is the limit for carrying in an enclosure not made for living in.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is a fragment. The start of the question ('if so, why may one carry there only...') is on the previous page. Read it as the punchline of a challenge, not as a statement on its own.

phrases.english: [why may one carry there] only within two beit se'a!
phrases.notes: Ends the question 'אי הכי, אמאי אין מטלטלין בו...' from the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the tree-branch challenge from the previous page by attacking the answer of 'tied with הוצא ודפנא'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the tree branches are a valid tied מחיצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A truly valid enclosure should allow carrying in any size. The size limit implies the enclosure is not fully valid.

steps.title: A dwelling used for the outside air
steps.stepSummary: The limit has nothing to do with the walls. This kind of space is a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, and any such space is limited to a בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a dwelling whose use is for the open air, and in any dwelling whose use is for the open air, one may carry only within בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The size limit comes from how the space is used, not from weak walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The area under the tree is not a real home. People use it as a base for the open space around it, like for shade or for watching the fields. The rule for such a space is that carrying is allowed only up to a בית סאתים. So the walls can be fully valid and the size limit still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Its use is for the open air outside it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea in הלכות שבת. The amount of space you may carry in can depend on what the space is used for, not only on whether its walls are valid.

phrases.english: Because it is a dwelling
whose use is for the open air,
and any dwelling whose use is for the open air,
one may carry in it only within two [beit] se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the reason for the limit: it comes from the type of space (its use), not from weak walls.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The size limit shows the tied branches are not a fully valid מחיצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The branches are a valid מחיצה. The limit applies because the space is a דירה שתשמישה לאויר.

steps.title: Proof from standing grain around a reaped field
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone spending שבת in a reaped area surrounded by uncut grain may walk the whole area plus 2,000 אמות. This treats the grain as a valid wall even though grain sways in the wind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who made his שבת place on a mound ten handbreadths high, between four אמות and two beit se'a in size; and similarly in a hollow ten handbreadths deep, between four אמות and two beit se'a; and similarly in reaped grain with uncut stalks surrounding it — he may walk the whole of it and 2,000 אמות outside it. Even though [the stalks] sway back and forth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test the rule that a swaying wall is not a מחיצה. The last case in this ברייתא seems to accept stalks of grain as a wall, even though grain moves in the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person on שבת gets four אמות plus 2,000 אמות. If his spot is enclosed, the whole enclosure counts like four אמות. The mound and the hollow are enclosed by a natural ten-טפח drop. The surrounding uncut grain is treated the same way. Since grain sways, this seems to show that a swaying wall does count as a מחיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source brought as proof
A hollow / cavity in the ground

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get lost in the mound and hollow cases. The proof comes only from the last case, the grain stalks. Those are the ones that sway.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who rested on Shabbat on a mound that is ten [handbreadths] high,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: and it is from four cubits up to two beit se'a,
and similarly in a hollow that is ten deep,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת עַד בֵּית סָאתַיִם,
phrases.english: and it is from four cubits up to two beit se'a,
and similarly reaped grain
with stalks surrounding it —
he may walk all of it
and outside it two thousand cubits.
Even though [the stalks] sway back and forth!
phrases.notes: The inference: swaying stalks are still treated as a wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the tree case is resolved, the גמרא brings a second source that seems to accept a swaying wall.
steps.raayaObject: That a swaying partition is a valid מחיצה (against the rule that a wall that can't stand in a normal wind is invalid)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about תל, נקע, and קמה קצורה surrounded by שבולות

steps.title: The stalks were tied too
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. In the grain case too, the stalks were tied with הוצא ודפנא so they don't sway.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, [it is] where he made it [firm] with palm leaves and laurel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the grain. It gives the same answer it gave for the tree branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is read as talking about stalks that were tied together with tough leaves so they stay in place. Tied stalks don't sway, so the case does not prove that a swaying wall is valid. The rule about walls that can't stand in a normal wind stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the tree and the grain cases are explained as tied-down partitions. So the rule stands: a wall that sways in a normal wind is not a valid מחיצה.

phrases.english: There too,
it is where he made it [firm] with palm leaves and laurel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי דְּעָבֵיד לֵיהּ בְּהוּצָא וְדַפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the grain case, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the stalks sway. The ברייתא can be read as talking about stalks tied firm with הוצא ודפנא.

steps.title: People on a מצוה mission are exempt from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Those traveling to do a מצוה are exempt from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Those sent on a מצוה are exempt from the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a new משנה with a new topic: who is exempt from sitting in the סוכה. The first group is שלוחי מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone busy doing one מצוה does not have to stop for the מצוה of סוכה. The גמרא will soon discuss the source and the limits of this exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: People traveling to do a מצוה

steps.whyThisMatters: This exemption is an application of the well-known rule עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה: someone busy with one מצוה is exempt from another. The גמרא will look for a Torah source for this rule.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Those sent on a מצוה —
are exempt from the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: a new משנה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלוחי מצוה are exempt from סוכה.

steps.title: The sick and their caretakers are exempt
steps.stepSummary: Sick people and those taking care of them are exempt from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sick and their attendants are exempt from the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second exempt group: the sick and the people taking care of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick person is exempt because being in the סוכה would cause him discomfort. His caretakers are exempt too, because they need to be with him to help him.

phrases.english: The sick and their attendants —
are exempt from the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second exemption listed in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sick and their caretakers are exempt from סוכה.

steps.title: A casual snack may be eaten outside the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: Casual eating and drinking may be done outside the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may eat and drink casually outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a different kind of rule: not who is exempt, but which kind of eating does not need a סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a real, set meal (קבע) must be eaten in the סוכה. A snack or casual eating (עראי) may be done outside. The גמרא will later define how much food counts as עראי.

keyTerms.meaning: Casual, temporary (as opposed to a set meal, קֶבַע)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three rules: שלוחי מצוה are exempt, the sick and their caretakers are exempt, and casual eating (עראי) may be done outside the סוכה.

phrases.english: One may eat and drink casually
outside the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final ruling of the same משנה. It shifts from exempt people to exempt kinds of eating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Casual eating and drinking (עראי) is allowed outside the סוכה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that those traveling for a מצוה are exempt from סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section on the new משנה begins. It asks where we learn that a person doing one מצוה is exempt from סוכה. This question sets up the next move, where a source will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (Step 5) stated a rule but gave no source. Here the גמרא asks for a Torah source for the principle that someone busy with one מצוה does not have to do another.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא on the new משנה.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's rule that those traveling for a מצוה are exempt from סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה quoted in Steps 5-7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for the rule that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from other מצוות.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns the exemption from the verse of שמע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'בשבתך בביתך' and 'ובלכתך בדרך' as excluding someone busy with a מצוה and a חתן from קריאת שמע. A man marrying a בתולה is exempt, but a man marrying an אלמנה is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'When you sit in your house' excludes someone busy with a מצוה. 'And when you walk on the way' excludes a groom. From here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt, and one who marries a widow is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that learns from the פסוק of קריאת שמע that a person busy with a מצוה is exempt. It adds a practical rule about a חתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists the times when one says שמע: sitting at home and walking on the road. The ברייתא reads these as ordinary personal activities, so someone busy with a מצוה, such as a חתן, falls outside them. The same principle then gives the exemption from סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: When you sit in your house (from the פסוק of שמע)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about קריאת שמע, not סוכה. The גמרא borrows the general principle (someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה) and applies it to סוכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the general rule עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה, which applies across many areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"When you sit in your house"
phrases.notes: From דברים ו:ז, the times for saying שמע.

phrases.english: — excluding one who is busy with a מצוה,
"and when you walk on the way"
— excluding a groom.
From here they said:
One who marries a virgin is exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from שמע on the wedding night.

phrases.english: and one who marries a widow is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of קריאת שמע excludes someone busy with a מצוה and a חתן, which shows that being busy with a מצוה exempts a person from another מצוה.

steps.title: How does the verse show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק imply that a חתן is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the implication? (How is this learned from the verse?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the פסוק actually shows this exemption, since nothing in it obviously mentions a groom. This question sets up רב הונא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated its conclusions without explaining them. The גמרא wants to see the exact logic that turns 'walking on the way' into an exemption for someone busy with a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the implication? How is this shown?

phrases.english: From where is it inferred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא's reading in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק's words imply an exemption for a חתן or anyone busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: רב הונא: like a voluntary trip
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the obligation covers activity similar to 'the way,' which is a voluntary trip. So only voluntary activity obligates, which excludes someone busy with a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Like 'the way.' Just as the way is voluntary, so too all cases are voluntary. This excludes this one, who is busy with a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. The 'way' in the פסוק is an optional trip, so the obligation to say שמע applies only to people doing optional things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא compares all obligated situations to the example in the פסוק. A trip on the road is usually a personal choice (רשות), so the פסוק describes people doing optional activities. Someone busy with a מצוה is not doing an optional activity, so he is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the derivation
Optional or voluntary, not a מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Like "the way."
Just as the way is voluntary,
so too all cases are voluntary,
to the exclusion of this one
who is busy with a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The way' is a voluntary trip, so the obligation of שמע is limited to voluntary activity, and someone busy with a מצוה is excluded.

steps.title: Maybe the verse includes a trip for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא. The פסוק does not say what kind of trip it means, so it could include a trip for a מצוה, and the Torah still requires שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are we not also dealing with someone walking to do a מצוה, and yet the Torah says he must recite שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's reading. The word 'way' could just as easily include someone traveling for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא assumed 'the way' means an optional trip. But the פסוק says nothing about the reason for the trip. If it covers מצוה trips too, the פסוק would actually obligate someone busy with a מצוה, which is the opposite of the ברייתא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with (a case of)...?

phrases.english: Are we not dealing with
one who is walking for a מצוה purpose,
and yet the Merciful One says he should recite!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָאָזֵיל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's explanation in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that 'the way' in the פסוק means only a voluntary trip.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not specify the trip's purpose, so it plausibly includes מצוה trips. That would obligate even someone busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: The word 'your' means your own personal activity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: the Torah could have said simply 'when sitting and when walking.' By saying 'your sitting' and 'your walking,' it limits the obligation to personal activity, so a מצוה trip is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'when sitting and when walking.' Why does it say 'when you sit' and 'when you walk'? It is in your own walking that you are obligated. But in walking for a מצוה, you are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the exemption by pointing to an extra detail in the פסוק: the word 'your' (the ending ־ךָ).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof no longer depends on what 'the way' usually means. It depends on the possessive form 'your.' 'Your walking' means a trip you take for yourself, so a trip done for a מצוה falls outside the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, let the verse say... (shows the wording is deliberate)

steps.whatToRemember: Saying שמע is tied to 'your' activities, meaning personal ones. When you are busy with a מצוה, you are exempt. This is the first source the גמרא offers for exempting מצוה travelers from סוכה. In step 19 the גמרא asks whether the rule is really learned from here or from a different source.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say
"when sitting and when walking";
what is the meaning of "when you sit" and "when you walk"?
It is in your own walking that you are obligated;
but in walking for a מצוה, you are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual precision: the possessive 'your' is extra and teaches a limitation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Walking on the way' could include any trip, even one for a מצוה, so that traveler would be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'your' limits the obligation to personal activity, so someone busy with a מצוה is exempt.

steps.title: Then why is one who marries a widow obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if anyone busy with a מצוה is exempt, a man marrying an אלמנה is also doing a מצוה and should be exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even one who marries a widow should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the rule just established, the גמרא challenges the end of the ברייתא, which said that a man who marries an אלמנה is obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the exemption comes from being busy with a מצוה, marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה. So the ברייתא's distinction between a בתולה and an אלמנה seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from what was just said)

phrases.english: If so,
even one who marries a widow should also be exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ כּוֹנֵס אֶת הָאַלְמָנָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of Step 13 against the ruling in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a man marrying an אלמנה is obligated in שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying an אלמנה is also a מצוה, so under the principle of Step 13 he should be exempt.

steps.title: Marrying a virgin causes worry; marrying a widow does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חתן's exemption here depends on being preoccupied. A man marrying a בתולה is anxious and distracted, while a man marrying an אלמנה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who marries a virgin is preoccupied; one who marries a widow is not preoccupied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by pointing to a difference in state of mind between the two grooms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men are doing a מצוה. But for קריאת שמע, the חתן is exempt only when he is actually distracted. A man marrying a בתולה worries whether she will be found a virgin. A man marrying an אלמנה has no such worry, so he can concentrate and must say שמע.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean that marrying an אלמנה is not a מצוה. It still is a מצוה. The exemption here also needs the groom to actually be distracted, which is an extra condition in this specific case.
steps.whatToRemember: A חתן is exempt from שמע only when he is truly preoccupied: one who marries a בתולה is exempt, and one who marries an אלמנה is obligated.

phrases.english: One who marries a virgin is preoccupied,
phrases.notes: He worries he may discover she is not a virgin.

phrases.english: one who marries a widow is not preoccupied.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases based on the groom's mental preoccupation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any groom doing the מצוה of marriage should be exempt, including one who marries an אלמנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The groom's exemption from שמע applies only when he is actually distracted, as with a בתולה, and not with an אלמנה.

steps.title: Should every distracted person be exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 15. If being distracted is what exempts the חתן, then a man whose ship just sank, who is also very distracted, should be exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that anyone who is distracted is exempt? If so, a man whose ship sank at sea is also distracted. Should he be exempt too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason given in Step 15, that the חתן is exempt because he is distracted. It gives an example that seems silly: a man whose ship sank.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 made being distracted the reason for the exemption. If that is the whole reason, then any stressed person should be exempt from קריאת שמע. A man who lost his ship is clearly stressed, and it sounds wrong to exempt him, so the reason looks too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: So too, also (often used to say 'is it really so?!')
But if that is so, then… (introduces an unwanted result)

phrases.english: And wherever one is preoccupied,
is he indeed exempt?!
But if that is so,
one whose ship sank at sea
who is preoccupied, should he also be exempt?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דִּטְרִיד, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 15 (being distracted).
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חתן is exempt because he is distracted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If distraction is enough to exempt someone, then any upset person, like a man whose ship sank, would be exempt. That seems unacceptable.

steps.title: A mourner still has to keep the מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks an escape. Someone might answer that yes, the ship owner is exempt. But רב said an אבל, who is surely very distracted, must keep every מצוה except תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say 'yes, he really is exempt,' didn't רבי אבא בר זבדא say in the name of רב: A mourner must keep all the מצוות of the Torah except תפילין, because the Torah calls תפילין 'splendor'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its challenge stronger. It shuts down the answer 'fine, the ship owner is exempt too' by quoting a ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is about as distracted and pained as a person can be. Yet רב says he must keep every מצוה, including קריאת שמע. His one exemption, תפילין, is for a special reason: תפילין are called 'פְּאֵר' (splendor), which does not fit a mourner. So distraction alone does not exempt anyone, and the question about the חתן comes back even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (heading off a possible answer)
תפילין, the boxes worn on the head and arm
Splendor, glory (a name the Torah uses for תפילין)

steps.confusionAlert: The אבל is exempt from תפילין because of the word 'פְּאֵר', not because he is distracted. That is exactly why his case proves that distraction by itself does not exempt.

phrases.english: And if you say that indeed, so it is,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say that Rav said:
A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות
stated in the Torah
except for tefillin,
as 'splendor' is stated regarding them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of Step 16 by ruling out the answer 'yes, he is exempt.'
steps.raayaObject: That being distracted does not exempt a person from מצוות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling, quoted by רבי אבא בר זבדא, that an אבל is obligated in all מצוות except תפילין.

steps.title: Distracted by a מצוה versus distracted by a personal matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חתן is distracted because of a מצוה, while the ship owner is distracted by a personal, non-מצוה matter. Only the first kind exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (the חתן), he is distracted by a מצוה. There (the ship owner), he is distracted by a personal matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by sorting distraction into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חתן's worry comes from the מצוה he is doing, so it falls under the rule that one busy with a מצוה is exempt. The ship owner's worry, like the אבל's grief, has nothing to do with a מצוה, so it does not exempt him. This fits Steps 11–13, where the exemption was tied to being busy with a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Preoccupation that comes from a מצוה
Preoccupation from a personal, non-מצוה matter

steps.confusionAlert: 'רשות' here does not mean the man chose to lose his ship. It just means his worry is a personal matter, not a מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: Distraction exempts only when it comes from a מצוה (חתן). Personal distress, like a sunken ship or mourning, does not exempt from קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Here he is preoccupied with the preoccupation of a מצוה,
there he is preoccupied with a voluntary (non-מצוה) preoccupation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא טְרִיד טִירְדָּא דְמִצְוָה, הָתָם טְרִיד טִירְדָּא דִרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Steps 16–17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) by the source of the distraction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any distraction exempts, so the ship owner and the אבל should be exempt too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only distraction that comes from a מצוה exempts. Personal distraction does not.

steps.title: Is the 'busy with a מצוה' rule really learned from here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need our פסוק to teach that one busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה. That rule is already learned from a different source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rule that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה, is it learned from here? It is learned from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the source of the rule from Steps 11–13. It is also setting up the ברייתא quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11–13 learned the exemption from the words 'בשבתך… ובלכתך' in the פסוק of קריאת שמע. The גמרא now says this rule already has another source, so learning it from קריאת שמע seems unnecessary. The 'other source' is the ברייתא brought in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One busy with a מצוה is exempt from another מצוה
It is derived from there (another source)

phrases.english: And the rule that one engaged in a מצוה is exempt from a מצוה —
is it derived from here?
It is derived from there,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָעוֹסֵק בְּמִצְוָה פָּטוּר מִן הַמִּצְוָה מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא? מֵהָתָם נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חתן question and questions the source used in Steps 11–13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the rule עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה from the פסוק of קריאת שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already learned elsewhere, so this פסוק seems unnecessary as a source for it.

steps.title: The other source: the men who were impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about the men who were טמא from a dead body and could not bring the קרבן פסח. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, they were the men carrying יוסף's coffin.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'There were men who were impure from a dead person…' Who were those men? They were the ones carrying יוסף's coffin. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the 'other source' it mentioned. It is a ברייתא that begins by identifying the men who were טמא, and it will continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These men missed the קרבן פסח because they were busy with a מצוה: carrying יוסף's coffin made them טמא. That they were not blamed shows that being busy with one מצוה exempts a person from another. Here the ברייתא only says who the men were; the rest of the discussion comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
יוסף's coffin, carried by the Jewish people in the desert
A תנא who gives this explanation

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
"There were men who were
impure by the corpse of a person, etc."
phrases.notes: במדבר ט:ו. They could not bring the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: Those men, who were they?
They were the bearers of Joseph's coffin,
the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: וַיְהִי אֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר הָיוּ טְמֵאִים לְנֶפֶשׁ אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the 'other source' that Step 19 referred to.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule עוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה is learned from somewhere other than קריאת שמע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on במדבר ט:ו about the men who were טמא (according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the bearers of יוסף's coffin) and missed the קרבן פסח.
